claims.text: Uncertainty quantification is challenging in free-form response generation with large language models.

Assuming utility is characterized by a similarity measure comparing a generated response with a hypothetical true response enables principled quantification of a language model's subjective uncertainty and calibration.
Epistemic uncertainty can be derived from a missing data perspective and characterized as an excess risk.
The proposed Bayesian decision theory methods for uncertainty quantification can be applied to black-box language models.
Epistemic uncertainty offers a promising deferral strategy for efficient data acquisition in in-context learning.

evidence.description: Experiments on question answering and machine translation tasks demonstrate that epistemic uncertainty provides an effective deferral strategy for data acquisition in in-context learning.

methodologies.name: Bayesian Decision Theory UQ Framework
methodologies.description: A framework mapping utility to a response-similarity measure to quantify subjective and epistemic uncertainty in natural language generation.

limitations.text: Task-specific uncertainties in free-form responses, such as semantic uncertainties, are difficult to define in general cases.
